newsitem.title: USA: Conoco reserves rose 3 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Conoco reserves rose 3 pct in 1996.

text.p: Conoco Inc said Wednesday its proven reserves increased by 53 million barrels of oil equivalent to 1.92 billion barrels in 1996, up almost three percent from 1995.
International proved reserves increased just over five percent, while U.S. reserves decreased slightly over one percent, the DuPont Co energy subsidiary said.
It said proved natural gas reserves increased by 6.4 percent to 5,676 billion cubic feet, while crude oil and liquids reserves decreased less than one percent to 973 million barrels.
The company said it added 267 million barrels of oil equivalent to worldwide proved reserves in 1996, replacing 125 percent of the oil and natural gas produced during the year.
Barrels of oil equivalent are calculated by dividing billions of cubic feet of natural gas by 6 and adding it to million barrels of crude and natural gas liquids.

"Conoco's ongoing efforts to restructure its asset base and make improvements in reservoir recovery and exploration efficiencies have enabled the company to increase its total reserves and replace more than it produced for the fourth consecutive year," said chief executive Archie W. Dunham.
He said performance of Conoco's United Kingdom affiliate and the company's U.S. drilling program were especially noteworthy.
"As they were last year, our U.K. operations were the pacesetters in replacing produced reserves, increasing total proved reserves by 12 percent and replacing 211 percent of production," Dunham said.
"In 1996, our U.S. drilling program resulted in 60.7 million BOE being added to our reserves making this the second most successful drilling program since 1983," he added.
